entry.title: comb project
entry.content:
Project comb: Topics:

  1. Product description Styling Hair comb Problem: regular standard combs work optimally with straight hair since it flow properties can be displayed in 2 dimensional. However curly hairs requires 3 dimesional. To be more precise, the comparison in description starts only after detangling; standard When brushing curly hairs using tradional comb [following is displayed in PowerPoint like boxes and arrows] Straight hair: comb straights hair in the 1 direction, hair clumps in the y direction, hair dryes and stays in shape Curly hair: comb curly hair in the 1 direction, hair clumps in the y direction, hair starts drying, hair starts twisting in groups determined by the clumps, natural curl force works against clump, causing clump to break and result messy hair. A simple alternative solution is to drench hair in water, this causes neighboring hair strands to clump, when it dries, the hair curling force doesn’t work against clump. [image of trad comb, with straight line highlighted] While this is a good solution, it forces users to drench their hair full and dry it which takes a very long time and demotivates most people. This is the problem we intent to solve by introducing comb which separates and clumps hair with minimum amount of water thus saving estimated 60% of users times. [image of comb clumping spaces in rectangular lines]

  2. Product requirements(important): material, weight, simplicity, minimum body parts, design for 3d printing Very light weight is imperative, simple in aesthetic, minimum body parts to insure higher lifespan. The product will be 3d printed with flexible material using SLS(use longer version) since product won’t suffer from anisotropic complications. Current printing material is Nylon 12 which is flexible to the required degree.

  3. Protoypes, overall and induvial mechanism There have being numerous comb design prototypes, with many mechanism considered. This section will detail some of them so as to show why the final result is logical and near excellence{c’mon be more humble}. List of considered mechanism: rigid teeth vs bending teeth made from smart material. Comb teeth are not parallel but are angled and expand from the center. A mechanism reduces the angle b/w teeth, this has the advantage of using thinner teeth and simpler parts but it lacks accuracy. Rotating teeth Switch mechanism: Latch + stick + bell crank/scotch yoke + spring Latch(bending stick with linear snap action) Latch(push-push mechanism) -Prototype 1 Pictures of first prototype[gearfest] Prototype 2 Images of second prototype [spiraling way to heaven] Prototype 3 Images of third prototype [layered skin]

  4. Material properties Nylon 12; flexible plastic, low water absorption.
  5. Simulation: fixture; detent mechanism There are 3 points that requires simulation; top fixture, detent mechanism, teeth-hair contact. Show top fixture simulation pictures; state material strain limits, compare and state chosen Show compliant detent mechanism, show that it either week or requires too much force. State that operating force is 1-3N Do a quick simulation on teeth-hair
  6. Topology optimization Do topology optimization. If you cant then remove this section
  7. Better design; compliant, statement of my limited knowledge Later mechanism
  8. Aesthetic [idk]

shax 0.1
entry.content:
Product description

Shax (also known as Jar) is an abstract strategy game with custodian capture rules, played on a 5X5 board. The game consists of two phases: a placement phase followed by a movement and capture phase. Shax is popular in East Africa, and while its exact origin is unknown, it is closely related to Seega, a traditional game from Egypt.

This demo showcases an AI engine for Shax, implemented using Monte Carlos tree search algorithm. Rather than solving the game exhaustively, the engine optimally traverses through the nodes to identify strong moves. The demo also includes visualization of the moves explored by MCTS with metadata attached to individual nodes.


Engine making

board state:

The state of the board can be formatted in to ways serialized or matrix. using matrix is much easier and more intuitive but is requires larger storage and higher stress in computation; with calculation literally in the thousands it’s wiser to use serialized format. {insert image here, showing both} the board is stored in 25 int array. the board also has meta data that are required which are: turn, last capture, current game phase; these take 3 slots thus the board becomes 28 int arrays.

Converting between serial and matrix back and forth is generally avoided, but in situations needed the code below is used.

The board has blue vs black piece with each piece having an identifier; blue goes from 1-12, black goes from 13-24; zero means slot is empty. when verifying if a move causes capture, u have to know between friend or foe.

In matrix format, knowing adjacent positions is intuitive. but in series format (FEN) it’s a bit tricky; Converting FEN to matrix and calculating adjacent positions then converting back to FEN defeats the purpose of serialization. To find adjacent in serialized position without any conversion, we use the following code; it’s also important to verify that ur not on any edges.

Most calculation related to board state constitutes of mixing and modifying the last 2 equations and delving into it is unnecessary.

Move Logic Pipeline


MCTS

Game decisions form a branching search space, too large to fully calculate. A greedy policy takes the immediate best reward but often fails long term. Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) tackles this by running simulated rollouts and updating value estimates at each branch. Its key innovation is balancing exploration and exploitation, much like modern AI agents do when learning from experience. Over many iterations, the search converges toward optimal strategies without needing prior training data.

In small games like tic-tac-toe, the state space is tiny enough that the full game tree can be pre-computed. But in larger games that scale toward PSPACE-hard or even EXPTIME-level complexity, the branching and depth explode, making exhaustive search impossible. This is where Monte Carlo Tree Search proves valuable: by running targeted simulations, it can handle decision spaces far beyond what brute-force methods allow.

Heuristic Board analysis

Relying only on capture value for scoring node is inefficient generally and outright fail in the first phase since it’s the placement phase. therefore it’s necessary to analyze the board and give heuristic value.

Currently there are 5 pattern we use, if they’re found in the board an extra value is give to the board. if the player is actively threatening a piece they also get point. if the player puts piece in negative positions they lose a point -negative positions marked Red X are position which block advantageous movement and most pattern have negative position-

The five patterns are as follow:

Knight control (+2pts), Rook control (+2pts), Solo corner control (+1pt), Duo corner control, Trio edge control (+2pts).

Every instance of the game board can be analyzed and given a score. for example this board below has score of xyx from blue side.

MCT UI

little monty and big monty
MCTS UI tree was built with unity UI toolkit which uses CSS Flexbox-like styling system. In this section the challenge was less about the tool but how to display it in manner that is informative and user friendly, avoiding cluttering etc.
That’s why we decided to use tree system with minimized text and added indicator on the board to avoid using information board[find better word].


Miscellaneous

[my version]

There were numerous problems faced in making the engine. Initially there was no simulation in the MCTS this caused the moves to be uninspiring and predictable while also reducing entropy. there was also the cases of AI becoming too defensive and other cases of it becoming careless about the danger; this hubris was due to the lack of Bi-turn backpropagation. And finally the hardest problem to solve OOM-out of memory-. In this section, will go through them in details.

During the early development of the engine, the AI was too defensive because all backpropagation stages were values the same, this was fixed by adding exponential decay along the backpropagation. and in the case were the AI was too offensive, this was triggered because half the nodes are disproportionate [ends without complete bi-turn cycles]. For example, if the AI count odd moves like ‘AI->human->AI’ it would assume it has advantage when in reality it should’ve considered the following opponents move. this was a particularly hindering problem and it’s solution is to stop backpropagation only at even moves.

OOM or ‘out of memory exception’ was particularly re-occurring problem in the web build of the engine. this was due to the reality that AI algorithm require a huge memory. My jar-engine suffered from 1.5 GB of memory spike after every calculation. this was because every node was this was because i had a heuristic function with 10 list<int[2]>, each list containing 4 int[2]; the heuristic function is called 5 times per node and there are 30,000 node. this calls for 6 million heap allocation causing ludicrous memory spike. the solution was to switch from list to struct to avoid constant allocation followed de-allocation in the heap. and any list which couldn’t be changed to struct were kept with the use scratchpad which is basically reusing the same list by manually clearing it with each use. these 2 solutions made the spike to a 100 MB per MCTS calculation reducing 75% from the original spike.

[gpt version]

Several challenges arose during the development of the engine. Initially, the absence of simulation in the MCTS resulted in moves that were predictable and uninspiring, with reduced entropy. In some cases, the AI became overly defensive, while in others it neglected potential dangers; this inconsistency stemmed from the lack of bi-turn backpropagation. The most difficult issue, however, was out-of-memory (OOM) errors. In this section, each of these problems will be discussed in detail.

During the early stages of development, the AI often played too defensively because all stages of backpropagation were weighted equally. This issue was resolved by applying exponential decay along the backpropagation path. Conversely, when the AI played too aggressively, the problem stemmed from nodes that ended prematurely, without completing a full bi-turn cycle. For example, after a sequence like AI → Human → AI, the engine mistakenly assumed an advantage, without accounting for the opponent’s next move. This significantly hindered performance. The solution was to restrict backpropagation to even-numbered moves, ensuring that evaluations always reflected complete cycles.

Out-of-memory (OOM) exceptions were a recurring problem in the web build of the engine, primarily because AI algorithms demand substantial memory. The jar-engine in particular experienced spikes of up to 1.5 GB after each calculation. This occurred because the heuristic function used ten List<int[2]>, each containing four int[2]. Since the heuristic was invoked five times per node across 30,000 nodes, the process required approximately six million heap allocations, leading to severe memory overhead.

To address this, two optimizations were introduced. First, lists were replaced with structs wherever possible to avoid repeated allocation and deallocation on the heap. Second, for lists that could not be converted, a “scratchpad” approach was adopted—reusing the same list by manually clearing it between uses. These changes reduced the memory spike to about 100 MB per MCTS calculation, a 75% improvement compared to the original implementation.

little monty and big monty use to go to the forest together to play, until one day big monty lost little monty and he was afraid to go back home without him. he started howling, yawning, puffing and making every sound untill medium monty appeared from the trunk of the big tree. medium monty was slimy and he promised to find little monty if big monty gave him the munchies. big monty hastly agreed not knowing what it was.

medium monty leaped through the trees and effortlessly brought back weeping little monty. big monty became joyous, but unbeknownst to him medium monty turned into a big monkey and demanded the munchies. big monty afraid vehemently pointed to his home and said “munchies there” medium monty sprinted away. big monty and little monty started running back to the house as it was dark and upon entering the house. they saw the horror in their mothers eye exclaiming “mother of all monties help, strike thee thythou, helio help medium monty is infecting the munchies”. as she completed her cries the roof opened and mother of all monties appeared carrying the entirety of munich in one hand and the chronicle of monties in the other; she looked appalled by the disgusting look medium monty gave her, as she was about to cast him away he wailed for the mother of all munchies, crying he said “hmmm aughhds ohoh ohho ohho”.

act 3

hearing the call all munchies in the room started shaking the belly of medium monty started shaking and shaking and bursted open there she appeared the most majestic looking munchies. little monty could not resist the smell and started biting and eating the mother of all munchies. a sacred law was broken as it was forbidden to eat what thou casted. the whole family was executed as an offering next day. the end

new confused branch You’ll find this post in your _posts directory. Go ahead and edit it and re-build the site to see your changes. You can rebuild the site in many different ways, but the most common way is to run jekyll serve, which launches a web server and auto-regenerates your site when a file is updated.

Jekyll requires blog post files to be named according to the following format:

YEAR-MONTH-DAY-title.MARKUP

Where YEAR is a four-digit number, MONTH and DAY are both two-digit numbers, and MARKUP is the file extension representing the format used in the file. After that, include the necessary front matter. Take a look at the source for this post to get an idea about how it works.
